digest.component_or_area: rebar reconciler — inbound link removal and graph link store
propositions: Link removal is pair-scoped (takes no relation argument) while link addition is relation-scoped (keyed on target_id + relation), causing asymmetry where one ordered pair can hold two net-active differently-related deps (e.g. blocks + relates_to) but removal only targets the most recent

Guard G5 in _inbound_unlink_one declines with a permanent non-converging log line when an inbound remove record's named relation does not match the pair's net-active relation, because outbound deduping on vendor type prevents the outbound re-add that would normally suppress the inbound remove in G4

Inbound link removal never converges for a double-related pair when the outbound differ emits no link mutation (inbound-only application or direction-agnostic dedup collision) and the surviving remote link's vendor type collides with a local dep of the same type, leaving the pair's other relation stranded in G5 decline

The fix implements relation-scoped removal symmetric with relation-scoped addition: graph/_links.remove_dependency keyed on (target_id, relation) validates the relation, finds the most recent net-active LINK with that exact key, and writes the UNLINK event, with _get_link_info gaining an optional relation filter
CLI rebar unlink <id1> <id2> [relation] gains an optional relation argument; with no relation, existing pair-scoped most-recent behavior is unchanged for backward compatibility

When a removal names a relation with no matching net-active local link, it removes nothing and logs as a no-op, preserving the safety invariant that a removal never destroys a link the peer still carries
